sources.name: CPAN Security Advisory Database (CPANSA) export
sources.notes: Current export inventory: 1060 distinct advisory IDs across 440 distributions (2052 distribution-level records). Primary Perl-specific seed source; records provide affected/fixed ranges and optional CVEs/references.

sources.name: CPANSA per-distribution YAML records
sources.notes: Human-reviewable source records underlying much of the export. Advisory candidates link to the matching dedicated YAML when retained under its distribution name; two link to the authoritative export because no matching dedicated YAML path was present.

sources.name: CPAN::Audit / cpan-audit
sources.notes: Consumer and setup tool, not an independent corpus. It materializes the CPANSA knowledge base and can audit a distribution, installed tree, cpanfile, or cpanfile.snapshot.

sources.name: CPAN Security Group CNA announcements
sources.notes: Authoritative Perl/CPAN CNA coordination and announcement channel. Use to resolve or corroborate recent CPAN CVEs; no fixed, machine-counted snapshot was taken for this catalog.

sources.name: CVE List V5
sources.notes: Official CVE record archive for alias and reference reconciliation. It is not a Perl-filtered benchmark inventory, so no case count is claimed here.

sources.name: NIST National Vulnerability Database CVE API
sources.license: NIST terms; check current use conditions
sources.notes: Supplementary CVE and change-history source. Older records may have less detail according to NVD; use to corroborate, not to infer a patch or runnable trigger.

sources.name: GitHub Advisory Database
sources.notes: Supplemental GHSA/CVE reference source. Its documented supported ecosystem list does not include CPAN, so it must not be treated as a complete Perl corpus.

sources.name: OSV.dev
sources.notes: Aggregator/API useful for aliases and affected-version enrichment. Correct data at the upstream database; no Perl/CPAN-specific case count is claimed.

sources.name: Canonical public GitHub repository pool
sources.notes: Eighteen canonical repositories were resolved with the GitHub repository API. These are diversity seeds only and are explicitly cataloged as project_candidate entries rather than vulnerabilities.
